To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of 3D computer vision methods for the extraction of ASL features yields a 92.3% recognition rate for continuous sentences.

(a) 3D data can be used to extract ASL movement parameters; (b) the second approach yields the best recognition results; (c) the recognition rate of 3D data is comparable to the recognition rate of the data from the 'Flock of birds' sensor, but the former has the advantage of being more easily accessible; and (d) our approach can be used to recognize ASL sentences in a continuous fashion.

3D computer vision methods can be used to obtain accurate 2D and 3D movement data of ASL sentences; that the HMMs trained on these features yield recognition rates that are competitive with the best published results for ASL recognition; that context-dependent HMM training is not as effective as modeling transient movements between sign; and that our recognition rates can be improved further by adding more context-dependent models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system for continuous ASL recognition, based on 3D data, which is able to recognize ASL signs and sentences in a real-time environment.
developing a robust ASL recognition system, which is capable of recognizing a wide variety of sign language sentences.
the development of a system for continuous ASL recognition that can be used for real-world applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of 3D motion parameters for ASL recognition is feasible and that the use of context-independent HMMs, which are trained on the transient movements between signs, gives the best performance.
we have successfully adapted HMMs for ASL recognition, using 3D computer vision methods.
the proposed method is a promising approach to continuous ASL recognition, and it has the potential to be extended to other sign languages.

we have successfully applied 3D computer vision techniques for ASL parameter extraction and have shown that ASL can be recognized by HMMs, which use these parameters as features.

The main takeaway from our work is that

3D computer vision methods can be successfully integrated in HMM-based sign language recognition systems, and the resulting system can be used for real-time recognition of continuous sign language sentences.
3D computer vision methods are a promising approach for continuous ASL recognition, which can lead to a better understanding of the ASL phonology.
HMMs can be adapted for ASL recognition using 3D movement data and the proposed methods can be used to improve recognition accuracy.
